We don’t own GPUs or data centres. A resource we haven’t re-checked in two weeks doesn’t get quoted.

Four places a compute deal usually gets stuck

  • Plenty of quotes, no way to tell which are real

    The same batch gets relayed through several people. Stock on hand, future allocations and units already sold all look alike.

    What we doWe grade every resource by how well it’s verified and only quote what we’ve checked recently.

  • GPUs without a rack, racks without power

    Servers, rack space, power and network sit with different parties. One missing piece keeps the cluster dark.

    What we doWe line up arrival dates, rack positions and power-on dates in one schedule before anyone signs.

  • Signed, then nothing ships

    A middleman takes the order without supply behind it, and you find out a month or two later.

    What we doOur quote states the supply status, the delivery conditions, and what happens if delivery fails.

  • Compliance questions surface at the last step

    Nobody pinned down the end user or location, and the supplier or data centre stops the deal before delivery.

    What we doWe confirm end user, location and use in writing first. Requests that don’t pass, we don’t take.

Four services, used alone or joined into one deal

GPU leasing and server procurement

Who it’s forAI companies, listed companies and research teams that need whole servers or clusters, deployed outside mainland China.

What we do

  • Match lease or purchase supply to your model, quantity, term and delivery location
  • Verify whether supply is on hand or a future allocation, and the real lead time
  • Help settle term, prepayment and delivery conditions

What you get

A written quote stating supply status, commercial terms, delivery date and validity.

AI data centre colocation and development

Who it’s forTeams with their own hardware looking for rack space, and developers or investors building AI data centres in Southeast Asia.

What we do

  • Source rack space, power and liquid-cooling capacity around Singapore, currently mainly Malaysia and Batam, Indonesia
  • Check power capacity, permit status and power-on dates
  • Connect data centre projects with colocation customers, contractors and operators

What you get

A side-by-side sheet of rack and power options, with power-on dates and billing start.

Fit-out and operations

Who it’s forData centre owners, main contractors and hardware owners that need local crews and on-site staff.

What we do

  • Electrical, low-voltage and security works
  • Server racking and data centre relocation
  • Ongoing operations under an agreed SLA
  • For high-density liquid cooling and GPU cluster networking we bring in a specialist team per project and name who is responsible

What you get

An itemised scope, schedule and operations SLA, carried out by local engineering teams we work with long term.

Enterprise cloud and model APIs

Who it’s forCompanies with significant monthly cloud spend, and AI application teams calling large models through public cloud.

What we do

  • Set up enterprise accounts, discounts and billing on major public clouds through authorised resellers
  • Help you enable model APIs properly on those cloud platforms
  • Only for a company’s own normal usage; model services are available only where their providers support them

What you get

A discount proposal and a clear billing structure.

From first conversation to a running cluster

  1. Describe the requirement

    Model or compute size, quantity, location, target go-live date, lease or buy.

  2. Confirm end user and use

    Written confirmation of who will use it, where, and for what. If this step fails, we stop here.

  3. Match and verify resources

    We check supply, rack space, power and crew availability one by one and grade each.

  4. Quote and way of working

    A written quote with validity, delivery conditions and which of the two models applies.

  5. Sign and deliver

    Arrival, racking, commissioning and power-on, accepted against contract milestones.

  6. Operate and renew

    Operations under the SLA. Before the term ends we agree renewal, expansion or exit.

The rules we apply to every deal

We don’t yet have client work we can name publicly. These are the rules we follow on every deal, and you can check each one as we work together.

Every resource gets one of four grades. Only the top two are quoted

  1. HearsayNever quoted
  2. VerbalNever quoted
  3. Written quoteQuoted to clients
  4. Seen or confirmedQuoted to clients

Any resource not re-checked within two weeks drops out of our quotes.

  • Compliance first

    For GPU requests we confirm end user, location and use in writing before discussing supply.

  • A clear role

    On every deal we state whether we are introducing or contracting, and where our fee comes from.

  • In writing

    Supply status, delivery dates and what happens on non-delivery go into the quote and the contract.

What we don’t do

  • Supply or tranship to countries, regions or end users restricted by export controls
  • Act as a nominee buyer or contracting party on someone else’s behalf
  • Quote supply we haven’t verified
  • Support model distillation, resale of personal subscriptions, or gambling businesses

Questions we hear often

Is there a minimum order?

There’s no fixed threshold. The smallest workable size depends on the specific supply and site, and suppliers usually prioritise whole batches and longer terms. Tell us the quantity and we’ll say plainly whether it can be done.

How long until we’re live?

It depends on whether supply is on hand or a future allocation, and when the site powers on. The quote gives a date for each stage. We don’t make blanket promises.

Why are there no prices on this site?

GPU lease and server prices move quickly with the market, term, prepayment and quantity. A published number is stale within days. We quote in writing against your conditions, with a validity date.

Does NOURRA own GPUs or data centres?

No. We assemble verified third-party resources. When NOURRA is the contracting party, NOURRA is responsible to you for delivery.

Can equipment be shipped to mainland China or other controlled destinations?

No. We only serve requirements used lawfully in permitted locations, and we confirm end user and location in writing.

How do you charge?

For introductions we charge a service fee. Who pays it and how it’s calculated is stated in writing beforehand. When NOURRA is the contracting party, our fee is part of the contract price.

Tell us what compute you need

Give us the model or size, quantity, location and target go-live date. That’s what lets us tell quickly whether we have a match.
